subject: Data locality, erasure workflow and region-affinity for Dedicated cluster

Subject: Questions on data locality & deletion for Dedicated cluster

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security team on Dedicated deployments before we escalate to procurement:

- Does the inference or KV cache ever leave the region when we enable region affinity (we need to demonstrate EU-only processing)?

We need this in writing for our security signoff. If you have a short checklist or a PDF we can include with the security questionnaire that would be great.

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on data locality & deletion for Dedicated cluster

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then actionable steps below. Attaching a short FAQ PDF.

1) Region affinity and runtime locality
- When you provision a Dedicated cluster with "region-affinity: eu" we schedule inference and KV/cache processes on compute instances that are physically in the selected EU region (e.g., eu-west-1).
- Control plane: by default the Redwood control plane is hosted (may be in a US region). If you require full EU residency for control plane metadata we offer a Private control plane option (VPC-hosted) as part of the Dedicated+Private package — that prevents metadata from leaving the EU.

2) Retention defaults and TTLs
- Request logs: default 90 days; configurable to 30/90/365 or custom via policy.
- Model inputs (payloads) and embeddings: default 30 days; can be set to 0 (no storage) or any TTL up to 3650 days via per-account policy.
- We support account-wide enforcement using policy templates we push during onboarding.

3) Deletion / erasure workflow
- Automated TTL: when TTL expires data is garbage-collected and overwritten on disk via our secure wipe process (zeroing + SSD secure erase where applicable).
- Manual certified erasure: we accept a signed erasure request from your security or legal contact. We then run the erase job with verification and provide:
  * an audit log of erase actions (job id + timestamps),
  * list of affected object keys,
  * a signed wipe certificate (PDF) confirming completion.
- For Dedicated nodes we also support ephemeral volume re-provisioning on decommission so no residual snapshots remain.

4) KMS / encryption
- BYOK: supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated clusters when using the Private control plane option; keys can be provisioned in your EU KMS and Redwood will accept KMS-wrapped keys for model input encryption and storage at rest.
- If you use Hosted control plane + Dedicated compute, we can offer Bring Your Own Key with an EU-backed KMS, but the control plane will still be able to see metadata unless you opt into Private control plane.

Next steps I suggest:
- I attached a 2-page FAQ that summarizes the above.
- If you want a written addendum that goes into the contract (data residency + erasure SLA) we can produce a one-page appendix and route to Legal.
- We can schedule a 30-minute technical call next week to walk your infra/security team through the BYOK flow and provide a timeline for implementing region-affinity on a Dedicated cluster.

Attachment: dedicated-data-locality-faq.pdf

Thanks — happy to get this into a doc for procurement.

— Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
